citation: Roe, E., Galbraith, A., Boudiab, L. D., & Johnson, B. S. (2019, December). The use of veteran-centric simulations in a nursing program. Clinical Simulation in Nursing, 37(C), 44-49. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecns.2019.08.003
thesis: A descriptive-comparative, one-group pretest/posttest study testing whether embedding Veteran-centric clinical simulations across a first-semester BSN curriculum measurably shifts students' self-reported confidence and comfort caring for Veterans, framed through Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Romer's deliberate-practice theory and reporting a significant pre/post gain (FE, p.44-48).

sections.title: Background
sections.summary: Motivates the study from Veterans' distinct health needs, low VA-system utilization (~29%), scarce VA clinical placements, and a literature gap (anecdotal, not rigorous empirical, support for Veteran-centric simulation); situates the VA Nursing Academy partnership and Joining Forces initiative (FE, p.44-45).

sections.title: Conceptual Framework
sections.summary: Frames the study via Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Romer's (1993) deliberate practice — 'effortful activities designed to optimize improvement' — extending its usual psychomotor/skills application into a perceptions-of-confidence-and-comfort outcome (FAITHFUL-Roe, p.45-46).

sections.title: Methods
sections.summary: Descriptive-comparative, one-group pretest/posttest, nonmatched design across four semesters (eight data-collection points) at a ~450-student Midwestern U.S. BSN program; first-semester students in Veteran-centric simulations (41% of that semester's simulation load, six scenarios per Table 1); confidence/comfort measured via Lippman & Ozment's 12-item Likert instrument (alpha=.901) (FAITHFUL-Roe, p.45-46).

sections.title: Results
sections.summary: N=325 pre / 282 post; total mean score rose 32.7 (SD 7.2) to 38.1 (SD 5.0), t=10.7, p=.00; 10/12 items improved significantly; the two VA-clinical-experience-specific items did not reach significance; debriefing/course-evaluation feedback reported increased likelihood of asking about and thanking Veterans for service (FAITHFUL-Roe, p.47-48).

sections.title: Limitations
sections.summary: One-group pre/post design (no control group), an under-validated/unpublished instrument, no open-response data, uncontrolled extraneous Veteran contact outside the simulations, and ~13% attrition/survey fatigue (FE, p.48).

sections.title: Discussion
sections.summary: Reads the gain as evidence deliberate-practice-based simulation can shift affective/confidence outcomes, not only psychomotor skill, consistent with Breitkreuz et al. (2016) and Fossen & Stoeckel (2016); situates the finding against NCSBN's National Simulation Study without claiming clinical-hour substitution; calls for continued Veteran-centric simulation and longitudinal study (FE, p.48-49).

constructs.label: self-efficacy
constructs.sourceTerm: perceptions of confidence and comfort caring for Veterans
constructs.treatment: Sole measured outcome; 12-item Likert total and per-item means, pre vs. post (FAITHFUL-Roe, p.46-48).

constructs.label: learning outcomes: procedural / skills
constructs.treatment: Treated only as deliberate practice's traditional target, set up as an explicit contrast to this study's affective-outcome extension; not itself measured (FAITHFUL-Roe, p.45-46).

conditions.design: descriptive-comparative, one-group pretest/posttest, nonmatched (no control/comparison group)
conditions.setting: ~450-student Midwestern U.S. BSN program, first-semester students, four semesters / eight data-collection points
conditions.instrument: Lippman & Ozment (2013, unpublished) 12-item Likert 'Nursing Student Perceptions About Caring for Veterans' questionnaire; Cronbach's alpha = .901 (excluding two VA-clinical-experience items)
conditions.manipulation: Six scripted Veteran-centric simulation scenarios (41% of first-semester simulation load), spanning Korean Conflict/Vietnam/OEF/OIF Veterans and conditions (chronic pain/PTSD, respiratory distress, UTI, type-2 diabetes, interpersonal conflict, altered mobility) — Table 1
conditions.mediaConditionColumnFit: ****** UNVERIFIED: in-person, non-digital simulation lab; manikin- vs. standardized/scripted-actor-based delivery not stated in text; does not cleanly map onto any §3 media-condition column (IVR/desktop-3D/2D/screen-based virtual patient)
conditions.effectDirection: positive, statistically significant total-score gain (t=10.7, p=.00); 10/12 items significant

concepts.gloss: Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Romer's (1993) 'effortful activities designed to optimize improvement'; here extended from psychomotor skill to an affective/confidence outcome (FAITHFUL-Roe, p.45-46).
Curriculum-embedded scripted clinical scenarios featuring Veteran patients/family, designed collaboratively with VA Medical Center educators per INACSL Standards (FE, p.45-46).

interlocutors: Ericsson, Krampe & Tesch-Romer (1993) — deliberate practice theory
Cooper, Andrew & Fossey (2016) — literature review calling for rigorous empirical study
Maiocco, Stroupe, Rhoades & Vance (2018) — clinical nurses' uncertainty caring for Veterans
Tosterud, Hedelin & Hall-Lord (2013) — simulation as safe-environment practice
Dickinson, Hopton & Pilling (2016) — NCSBN National Simulation Study

tensions.label: no-control-group gain vs. causal claim
tensions.note: A large, significant one-group pre/post gain is compatible with maturation, extraneous Veteran contact, and non-simulation confounds the authors themselves concede (p.48); relevant caution for Strand-D's broader 'simulation beats no-intervention' debate axis (P/anticipatory-application).
